name: Naaman
overview: Naaman is a male descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, noted specifically as a son of Bela and possibly a grandson of Benjamin. He is mentioned among the sons of Israel who went to Egypt, highlighting his place in the early genealogies of the Israelite people. His identification within the tribe of Benjamin situates him within the foundational history of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Naaman means "pleasantness," reflecting a Hebrew proper name given by human parents rather than directly by God. This meaning may suggest a character or reputation associated with favor or agreeable qualities, though the text does not elaborate further.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Naaman as a son of Bela and a descendant of Benjamin, establishing his lineage within the tribe of Benjamin. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are noted in the biblical record provided.
scriptureSignificance: Naaman's significance lies in his inclusion in the genealogical lists that trace the descendants of Israel who migrated to Egypt. This places him within the broader narrative of God's covenant people and the unfolding history leading to the Exodus. His mention underscores the faithfulness of God's promises to the tribes of Israel and preserves the memory of the tribe of Benjamin's early generations.
